headline: Weekend Brief: US equity futures slipped as US-Canada trade tensions escalated and bond-yield worries persisted ahead PCE data, Nvidia earnings, and Jackson Hole
raw_text:
- US stock futures edged lower Sunday evening after the Dow (DIA)’s back-to-back weekly declines and persistent concern over elevated bond yields.
- The US imposed new 50% tariffs on roughly $20B of Canadian imports, including autos, dairy, alcohol, steel, consumer goods, and other industrial and agricultural products, after weekend trade talks collapsed.
- Canada vowed dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs starting September 8, heightening cost pressures for US-exposed companies and weighing on cross-border supply-chain plays, industrials, autos, agriculture, materials, and retail.
- Oil prices dipped about 1% on looming additional US sanctions on Iran and threats to the Strait of Hormuz, pressuring energy names while potentially easing broader inflation concerns if prices stabilize.
- Crypto-related stocks could see upside from Bitcoin (@BTC)’s weekend rally.
- Shein’s launch of an up-to-$1.8B Hong Kong IPO is drawing attention to fast-fashion and other tariff-impacted consumer names tied to global supply chains with US exposure.
- Monday’s US data calendar is light, featuring the Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 8:30 a.m. ET and Treasury bill auctions.
- Attention is shifting to mid-week PCE inflation data for a read on price pressures and the policy backdrop.
- Nvidia (NVDA) is scheduled to report pivotal Q2 earnings after the close on Wednesday, with markets focused on AI spending trends.
- The Jackson Hole symposium later in the week is in focus for signals on interest-rate policy, broader monetary strategy, and the economic outlook.
